Web Guide
When using vi.useFakeTimers() in Vitest, time is frozen unless you manually move it forward using methods like vi.advanceTimersByTime() or vi.advanceTimersToNextTimer(). If setInterval still fails to progress, the root cause may be pre-initialization in dependencies, Nuxt environment conflicts, a missing React act wrapper, or a known GitHub bug.

1. Manual Timer Advancement Required

By default, Vitest's fake timers freeze time to allow deterministic testing. To make setInterval trigger its callback, you must actively progress the clock in your test logic:
  • Advance by specific duration: Use vi.advanceTimersByTime(ms) to move time forward by a defined number of milliseconds.
  • Advance to the next event: Use vi.advanceTimersToNextTimer() to automatically jump to the next scheduled interval or timeout.
  • Run all pending tasks: Use vi.runAllTimers() to exhaust the entire timer queue.
  • Automatic advancement configuration: If you prefer time to flow naturally while still using mocked dates or utilities, you can set the shouldAdvanceTime configuration option to true within your fakeTimers config or pass it directly into vi.useFakeTimers({ shouldAdvanceTime: true }) to let time increment based on system time.

2. Common Integration Pitfalls & Fixes

Depending on your tech stack, setInterval might stall due to environment-specific behaviors:
  • React State & DOM Updates: If your interval modifies React state, the test environment may fail to register the changes. Ensure that your timer advancement code is wrapped inside an act() utility block so Vitest can notice the DOM changes. Misusing custom hooks with incorrect dependencies can also block your callback execution.
  • Nuxt and Server-Side Guardrails: When using defineVitestConfig in a Nuxt application, the framework overrides the default timer implementations to prevent server-side execution. If standard intervals are not triggering, a common workaround is to explicitly invoke the global browser scope using window.setInterval instead of calling setInterval directly.
  • Pre-initialized Dependency Bundles: If a third-party library imports and caches the native timer functions before vi.useFakeTimers() is invoked, Vitest won't be able to intercept them. To resolve this caching issue, you must configure module mocking or adjust your test.server.deps settings to ensure the module re-initializes after the fake timers are active.

3. Edge Cases & Known Limitations

  • Zero and Negative Delays: Be cautious when providing a delay of 0 or negative values to setInterval. Bug reports indicate that vi.advanceTimersByTime(1) may instantly complete or exhibit unexpected handling errors under these conditions.
  • Browser Mode Constraints: If you are running tests inside Vitest's experimental browser mode, fake timers can sometimes stall UI actions. In these scenarios, utilizing the vi.setTimerTickMode("nextTimerAsync") configuration option can help restore normal behavior.
Official Guides and Examples
Pass shouldAdvanceTime true to useFakeTimers to automatically advance time, or use advanceTimersByTimeAsync for asynchronous callbacks.
